about.body: The AJ-V8 is Jaguar Land Rover's second-generation V8 petrol engine, in production from 1998 to 2015. It was fitted to the Range Rover Sport L320 across two main configurations: the 4.2-litre supercharged V8 and the 4.4-litre naturally aspirated V8. This engine family represents the earlier generation of JLR V8s, preceding the later 5.0-litre AJ133 that would replace it in the model line-up. The L320 Range Rover Sport was the primary application for this engine in the Land Rover range, offered from launch in 2005 through to the model's replacement in 2013.

byModel.body: The Range Rover Sport L320 (2005–2013) carried the AJ-V8 in two distinct forms. The 4.2 SC V8 delivered supercharged performance, using a belt-driven supercharger to increase power output. The 4.4 V8 was the naturally aspirated option, offering the same basic engine architecture without the supercharger. Both variants share the same underlying block and timing chain system, but the supercharged application carries additional components — most notably the supercharger unit itself and its associated cooling system — that require specific attention during a rebuild.

compatibility.body: Because the AJ-V8 spans two distinct configurations — naturally aspirated 4.4-litre and supercharged 4.2-litre — compatibility comes down to confirming your exact variant and specification. A supercharged AJ-V8 from a Range Rover Sport isn't a drop-in match for a naturally aspirated version; the supercharger, ancillaries, and ECU mapping all differ. Before we quote or supply anything, we confirm your exact vehicle and specification by registration/VIN.
